ambiguities_declared: The TTHM and HAA5 rows in both the PE-sample acceptance-limits table and the minimum-reporting-level table have blank value cells; only their individual component compounds carry numeric values, so no aggregate numeric claim was made for the TTHM/HAA5 rows themselves.

The disinfectant residual methods table (§141.131(c)(1)) marks applicability with 'X' across multiple residual-type columns (FreeCl2, CombinedCl2, TotalCl2, ClO2) per method; decomposing each method-to-residual-type combination into a discrete claim was not attempted since the mapping is inherently multi-valued and better represented as the table itself rather than individual claims.

Paragraph (a)(2) is an incorporation-by-reference index listing numerous method-source documents, editions, and access URLs; it was not decomposed into individual numeric or qualitative claims since it does not itself state a monitoring or compliance requirement.

It is unclear from the text alone whether 'if approved by the State' in (c)(2) and the 'party approved by EPA or the State' language in (b)(3)/(c)(3) impose distinct state-specific procedural requirements beyond simple approval; this was left as a generic condition rather than guessed at.

verified_quotes.exact_text: Systems must use only the analytical methods specified in this section, or their equivalent as approved by EPA, to demonstrate compliance with the requirements of this subpart and with the requirements of subparts U and V of this part.
These methods are effective for compliance monitoring February 16, 1999, unless a different effective date is specified in this section or by the State.

Analyses under this section for disinfection byproducts must be conducted by laboratories that have received certification by EPA or the State, except as specified under paragraph (b)(3) of this section.

Analyze Performance Evaluation (PE) samples that are acceptable to EPA or the State at least once during each consecutive 12 month period by each method for which the laboratory desires certification.

Until March 31, 2007, in these analyses of PE samples, the laboratory must achieve quantitative results within the acceptance limit on a minimum of 80% of the analytes included in each PE sample. The acceptance limit is defined as the 95% confidence interval calculated around the mean of the PE study between a maximum and minimum acceptance limit of ±50% and ±15% of the study mean.
Laboratories that use EPA Methods 317.0 Revision 2.0, 326.0 or 321.8 must meet a 0.0010 mg/L MRL for bromate.
A party approved by EPA or the State must measure daily chlorite samples at the entrance to the distribution system.
If approved by the State, systems may also measure residual disinfectant concentrations for chlorine, chloramines, and chlorine dioxide by using DPD colorimetric test kits.
A party approved by EPA or the State must measure residual disinfectant concentration.

TOC samples must be acidified at the time of sample collection to achieve pH less than or equal to 2 with minimal addition of the acid specified in the method or by the instrument manufacturer. Acidified TOC samples must be analyzed within 28 days.
SUVA is equal to the UV absorption at 254nm (UV254) (measured in m- 1 divided by the dissolved organic carbon (DOC) concentration (measured as mg/L).
This filtered blank must be analyzed using procedures identical to those used for analysis of the samples and must meet the following criteria: DOC <0.5 mg/L.
UV absorption must be measured at 253.7 nm (may be rounded off to 254 nm).
4 If TTHMs are the only analytes being measured in the sample, then a PID is not required.
6 Ion chromatography & post column reaction or IC/ICP-MS must be used for monitoring of bromate for purposes of demonstrating eligibility of reduced monitoring, as prescribed in § 141.132(b)(3)(ii).

8 Amperometric titration or spectrophotometry may be used for routine daily monitoring of chlorite at the entrance to the distribution system, as prescribed in § 141.132(b)(2)(i)(A). Ion chromatography must be used for routine monthly monitoring of chlorite and additional monitoring of chlorite in the distribution system, as prescribed in § 141.132(b)(2)(i)(B) and (b)(2)(ii).

1 X indicates method is approved for measuring specified disinfectant residual. Free chlorine or total chlorine may be measured for demonstrating compliance with the chlorine MRDL and combined chlorine, or total chlorine may be measured for demonstrating compliance with the chloramine MRDL.
